DUPED BY NETSTAR

By: Nicky Troll | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Netstar dupes clients into thinking they have exclusive and private ground and air recovery teams – we investigate a string of irregularities behind a big corporate’s false promises.

Unique Selling Point:
- Consumers being screwed
- Corporates being called out on their lies
- Action packed footage

Summary:
Netstar restructured its recovery team business model – they gave contractors of 23 years the boot and opened the door to new blood – cutting costs and apparently improving their business model – but is that what’s really happening?

They’ve cut down recovery teams, appointed a contractor that employs plumbers, mechanics, active duty cops, unregistered and suspended PSIRA companies. And consumers are none the wiser – they’re still paying the same fees, but not getting the same service.

We lift the lid on apparent sub-standard service that leaving consumers bearing the brunt of it.

Further information:
Up until February 2019 Netstar used to have sub-contractors in each province with dedicated teams. They used to get a sizable retainer and be paid a minimal fee per call out. The number of teams were determined by Netstar. Some companies had worked for Netstar for 23 and 10 years respectively.

Last year, Netstar decided that they wanted recoveries teams to fall under one entity nationally and put out a tender.

The contract was awarded to a company called Rentrack – they have a national footprint – but it’s not exclusive to Netstar - they do recoveries for Matrix, C-Track and Tracker.

IRREGULARITIES
1. NOT EXCLUVIE RECOVERY TEAMS – NETSTAR PROMISE TO CLIENTS
- We have cases where multiple cars from different tracking companies were taken on the same day in May – four Netstar cars were lost. The other companies cars were recovered – same team – too many recoveries.
2. EMPLOYS COPS TO DO RECOVERIES – ILLEGAL FOR COPS TO DO OTHER WORK
3. EMPLOYEES NOT ALL PSIRA REGISTERED – REQUIREMENT OF NETSTAR
4. EMPLOYS PEOPLE WITH NO SECURITY HISTORY – A PLUMBER / A MECHANIC
5. SUB-CONTRACTS COMPANIES THAT HAVE BEEN SUSPENDED FROM PSIRA – RED FLAG!!!
6. DOES NOT HAVE ENOUGH FIREARMS REGISTERED WITH SAPS – SO THESE COMPANIES ARE USING PRIVATE FIREARMS
7. POLICE CLEARANCE FOR EVERYONE COULD NOT HAVE BEEN DONE – NETSTAR REQUIREMENT

* HOW DO WE KNOW THESE THINGS?
- We have an insider that works for the new company feeding us information of the recovery team whatsapp group and has first hand experience with these recoveries gone wrong.
- We have insiders in Netstar that have given us the recovery stats
- We have pulled the data of PSIRA’s online platform – it’s not a case of outdated information – these details are updated real time by companies themselves
- We have checked the firearm registration this week.
- We have audio recordings confirming employment



CASE STUDY 1
Balan Chetty’s Hilux was stolen in Durban in April – he had two tracking devices installed because he new the Hilux was a high risk vehicle. He has CCTV footage of this car being stolen. Netstar only picked up the car had been stolen an hour later despite having an Early Warning System installed – the car was not recovered – they are furious and outraged having learnt that they’ve been paying service that NEtstar no longer provides.

CASE STUDY 2
4 MAY – 4 Netstar cars were stolen in KZN – not one recovered – on the same day – the same recovery team recovered a car for C-Track. The customers are furious! Two of the cars belonged to Crawford College – Rentrack didn’t send a recovery team – firstly because they didn’t have a team available, secondly they said they will only go when a signal is received from the unit – despite it being reported by the clients – this would not have happened under the old system.

INSIDER
We have someone who works for the new company – he’s seen first hand how backwards everything has gone – how the one and only team they have in Durban purposely delays reporting recoveries to push up the hours they can charge for. He’s seen how many cars they are losing because they are servicing different companies and has personally spoken to the Netstar control centre who have complained about losses.

EX-EMPLOYEE
Will explain the danger and importance of properly trained recovery teams.

FORMER SUB-CONTRACTOR
Will explain the break down of how it used to work and what’s happening now as well as point out irregularities in the tender process.

CONFRONTS
The main confronts are NOT with the employees – but with the company that is subcontracting them – so we are putting the allegations to Rentrack. In terms of the employees, we are merely confirming that the teams are not qualified and using private fire arms. Rentrack has to answer for employing them and seemingly misleading Netstar. Essentially the unqualified people aren’t lying about their qualifications, it’s there for the world to see on the PSIRA public online platform – it’s Rentrack and essentially Netstar that didn’t do due diligence. This is how I think it could work best in terms of storytelling and trying to keep costs down as I also understand that travel budgets are limited and it won’t be possible to go to all these places (Uitenhage, Plett, Bloem & Durbs) to have a 10 min chat to these teams.

Netstar’s interview will focus on whether they aware of what is going is on with their new contractor – were they hoodwinked and what will they do to rectify the illegality and substandard service?


VISUALS
I have a lot of recent footage of action packed vehicle recoveries, re-enactments of hijackings and vehicle thefts – there is also a lot of CCTV footage of cars being stolen and hijacked – so visually it would be action packed and fast paced with new footage.

IRREGULARITIES – VISUAL DEVICE
Then to introduce the problem areas and unqualified teams I’d work with an editor to use a clever device using maps and their photos, bringing up qualifications and short comings in a slick graphic representation. We’d then have audio recordings that we use along with the graphic and audio wave to make it visually interesting.

Script:


STRUCTURE

VO: Vehicle crime is big business for syndicates – they brazenly target motorists every day. Across South Africa, on average 138 vehicles are stolen and 44 cars are hijacked every single day .

LINK: Vehicle Recovery Tracking is not a nice to have in South Africa any more, it’s become a necessity – for peace of mind and some insurers require it – but are consumers getting what they think they’re paying for?

VO: Keshia Chetty and Mabusi Khuzwayo’s cars had Netstar tracking devices. Both their cars were stolen in Durban in May. Both cars have not been recovered.

MABUSI: I just want to know how come it takes them three hours to get to the car INT3 M9
KESHIA: We only actually got an alert an hour after the vehicle was physical taken away from our yard. INT1 M6 END

VO: Keshia Chetty’s family Hilux was fitted with a Netstar Early Warning system and an additional back up unit. On the neighbour’s CCTV footage you can see the bakkie being moved down the road by the thieves – take note of the time – 22.56 .

KESHIA: After that we got a phone call around 23.40 to say, to ask whether my brother who is the primary driver of the vehicle was ok? And whether the vehicle was ok // for us that was a bit of a shock – because an early warning system means…
DEVI: it means early warning…
KESHIA: early warning, //INT1 M6

VO: The two tracking devices were recovered about 40 km away in Kwamakhutha, south of Durban, almost two hours after the vehicle was stolen.

Mabusi Khuzwayo’s Etios was stolen in the early hours of the morning. Although she didn’t have an early warning system, a battery tamper notification was picked up by Netstar at 02.15 am – the message went unnoticed, no teams were dispatched at the time. Mabusi only realised the car was missing just over an hour later.

MABUSI: I phoned Netstar to say the car is missing //it was half past 3 am INT1 M4

VO: Mabusi was told a team was dispatched. She picked up her car’s location on the Netstar app, about an hour away from Durban in iFafa. But the response team only located the unit over three hours later.

MABUSI: // the time they got to the car at 7, something to 7 the car was not there – //It took you this long to get to the car – what do you expect? INT1 M12

VO: What Netstar clients expect, is simply what they are promised. //

UPSOUND NETSTAR CALL CENTRE: +/- 01.29: “We still have the largest private dedicated air and ground service in Southern Africa.”

VO: According to their website their recovery teams are exclusive to Netstar, and their highly trained recovery personnel respond to incidents at immediate notice.

But things have changed in recent months – Netstar have a new national recovery contractor, Rentrak.

While Gauteng seems to be running more smoothly, there appears to be hiccups in some of the other provinces .

INSIDER: we do recoveries for several different tracking companies – not just Nestar. INT1 M11

VO: We spoke to an insider who does vehicle recoveries for Rentrak in KwaZulu Natal – for fear of retribution we have hidden his identity.

DEVI: Which one do you do first?
INSIDER: You do the one that comes first. // if you are doing a track for another company and a Netstar comes // Netstar will have to wait. INT1 M12

VO: Rentrak took over Netstar’s national recovery operations during March and April. The company provides recovery services to a number of tracking companies across South Africa.

Up until then, Dale Milcher exclusively did Netstar’s recoveries in Gauteng, Bloemfontein and Kimberly – he lost the contract after 22 years and had to close his doors at a cost of R2.5 million.

DEVI: do you feel that the best bidder won?
DALE: honestly? No.
DEVI: Isn’t this just a case of sourgrapes – you didn’t get the contract
DALE: // Sure I am upset, but it doesn’t change a thing // INT 1 M19 // the facts are the facts. INT 2 M33 // Their agents in the areas are doing work for everybody – some of them have got private jobs. // INT 1 M18//

LINK: Not everyone can do armed vehicle recoveries - there are rules and regulations guiding the industry – not only to safeguard the people doing the work, but to ensure that consumers get the best service .

VO: While PSIRA is the Private Security Industry Regulatory body - Netstar set their own ground rules in the Technical Mandatory Requirements section of their tender document:

“The bidder’s armed response officers must at least have a grade C security grading in line with PSIRA requirements as well as an armed response certification.”

This would apply to the contractor and its subcontractors.

Our investigation revealed that Rentrak uses some recovery agents that don’t meet those requirements - some of these agents work on Netstar Recoveries.

Rentrak supplied us with the PSIRA certificates for its subcontracted agents outside of Gauteng acknowledging that their “agents are not full time agents” and that they conduct other businesses such as farming. Of the 75 agents, only 22 complied 100% with the requirements .

VO: One of the people that appeared on the Rentrak Recovery Agents Whatsapp Group is Gordon van Tonder – an electrician and police reservist in East London – he has not been PSIRA registered or graded. He has yet to do a call out, but is on currently standby.

UPSOUND GORDON VAN TONDER – DEVI (CALLS TO AGENTS – CLIP….26)
TIME CODE 14.40.58
DEVI: // if you are involved in any vehicle recovery, you would have to be registered with PSIRA before you do that.
GORDON: I didn’t realise that // The chap you must be speak to is Darron Saayman – he’s got the contract 14.39.27
DEVI: Helping out?
GORDON: I’m help him out yah.

VO: Rentrak says that Gordon will not be dispatched until he’s done his registration and training.

Darron Saayman is sub-contracted by another Rentrak sub-contractor. He has a PSIRA E grade – while he is a police reservist with 15 years experience…. His E grade qualifies him just to do basic patrolling – not even access control guarding.

UPSOUND DARRON SAAYMAN - (CALLS TO AGENTS – CLIP….27) 14.44.55
DEVI: you are listed as an E grade at PSIRA, I’ve seen it – you need to have C grade – E is the bottom
DARRON: No, no I know that, just please listen to my side – we’ve done our C grade, //, the course reports would have submitted I don’t know how long that process takes…
DEVI: The point still remains you are doing recoveries for Rentrak and until PSIRA recognises what you have submitted to them – you are still on E grade
DARRON: Correct

VO: PSIRA is currently also investigating these apparent irregularities. Advocate Linda Mbana heads up law enforcement at the regulator. She says the rules are clear when it comes vehicle recovery.

ADV MBANA: You must have Grade C – if you have Grade C that means you can do armed response – but you must also do armed response courses as well as firearm courses – so it is a package. INT1 M46
DEVI: Why so tough?
ADV MBANA: risky

VO: We also discovered that 37 of Rentrak’s subcontracted agents currently have no armed response training listed on the PSIRA database. Rentrack declined an on-camera interview but in correspondence said that an unarmed agent does not need an armed response grading.

That would mean that of Rentrak’s 75 subcontracted agents, more than half are possibly doing recoveries unarmed.

But even then PSIRA requires all security personal doing response work, armed or not, to have response training.

Of the 75 subcontracted agents, at least 19 of them were listed as unemployed in the security industry.

LINK: Being listed on PSIRA as unemployed doesn’t sound like a big deal - but it means you shouldn’t be working in the security industry you certainly wont have access to a company issued fire arm, so you would either be carrying your own or go in unarmed.

VO: Even though our insider has had the appropriate training, he carries his own private firearm.

DEVI: Can you use your own private firearm?
ADV MBANA: // the employer, which is the business, the security service provider is supposed to furnish the employee // with firearms – the employee is not supposed to be utilising his or her private firearm. INT1 M36

VO: While Rentrak say that they have “no control over how PSIRA lists agents” - Adv Mbana says it’s the responsibility of employers to update employment status on the database

ADV MBANA: // in terms of our regulation 8 – it is a misconduct for a particular service provider not to indicate to us how many intakes that particular company has taken. INT1 M16

VO: Rentrack say that subcontracted agents must at all times comply with all laws and regulations.

They further stated that the bid process was lawful and has never been challenged. They deny any irregularities relating to their agents, stating that they have co-operated fully with the ongoing PSIRA investigation. They added that they are contractually prohibited from commenting on Netstar cases.

According to Rentrak, besides E grade Darron Saayman, all of their agents are PSIRA registered as grade C and above. But that’s not the case. Their own list revealed another four D grade agents.

Rentrak claimed these people were in the process of upgrading to C level. We checked the list of non-compliant agents with PSIRA, who confirmed that until applications are validated, the current gradings have been captured accurately.

Netstar’s Managing Director Pierre Bruwer agreed to an interview.

DEVI: Are you happy that your contractor has complied?
PIERRE: in terms of submissions – and the high level requirements of netstar perspective we were comfortable that Rentrak is the most suitable supplier of our recovery service – // 15.59.17
DEVI: Does netstar have a dedicated ground and air teams?
PIERRE: In certain areas we do, in other areas we share. // 14.58.50

VO: While Netstar’s recovery services through Rentrak are not 100% exclusive, the insider says it seems the size of the ground teams have also changed.

INSIDER: sometimes in the vehicle there is only one person – like the driver he will handle all the equipment and do the recovery on his own // INT1 M42 // there is no day shift or night shift – you work 24 hours a day INT1 M14

VO: In Netstar’s tender document the minimum services required were quite clear - at least two trained and armed security officers would be needed per ground team.

PIERRE: From a tender perspective we put out a guideline to say at least two people per team – in certain areas we require one, so it was merely a guideline. 15.03.06

VO: However, Netstar insists there are now more teams on the ground and that the recovery stats have improved with Rentrak.

Looking at KZN, there were 11 teams of two people, with day and night shifts in Durban, Pietermaritzburg and Richardsbay previously.

PIERRE: today we have 18 supporting us from a recovery vehicles 15.52
DEVI: two people?
PIERRE: not all of the them are two people, some of them one people – // 15.52.50 //the teams today could be a person supported by SAPS we refer to it as 18 teams on the ground 15.54.00

VO: We wanted to verify the information and requested detailed statistics along with the details of the new agents - during the interview Bruwer was more than willing to share this with us, but afterwards said that the specific information was confidential.

Netstar is adamant that their footprint has increased nationally.

DEVI: increased numbers – don’t comply
PIERRE: that’s the response that we are awaiting from PSIRA and Rentrak//16.31.46

VO: But clients like Keshia and Mabusi are still waiting for answers.

Bruwer is believes that Netstar complied in both incidents - he confirmed Mabusi’s case was being investigated as it appears the agent didn’t respond in time.

KESHIA: // I think it was a sense of being // taken for a ride – because you are lead to believe you are taking a contract for X but you’re actually getting Y // INT1 M7

VO: PSIRA says it’s committed to getting to the bottom of the allegations against Rentrak and its subcontractors and hope to wrap up their investigations soon.

ADV MBANA: // We don’t tolerate non-compliance// there is going to be fireworks. INT1 M57


END


 
PROMOS

PROMO 1
VO: Vehicle tracking device are a necessity in South Africa’s crime climate. But will your car be recovered? We investigate irregularities behind one big tracking company’s apparent false promises.

PROMO 2
VO: Clients are promised exclusive ground and air recovery teams for stolen vehicles, but a special investigation reveals irregularities behind one major tracking company’s recovery operations.

PROMO 3
VO: Exclusive ground and air recovery teams to recover your vehicle when it’s stolen - that’s the promise one tracking company makes to its clients, but is it what customers are getting?

VO: Vehicle crime is big business for syndicates – they brazenly target motorists every day. Across South Africa, on average 138 vehicles are stolen and 44 cars are hijacked every single day . LINK: Vehicle Recovery Tracking is not a nice to have in South Africa any more, it’s become a necessity – for peace of mind and some insurers require it – but are consumers getting what they think they’re paying for? VO: Keshia Chetty and Mabusi Khuzwayo’s cars had Netstar tracking devices. Both their cars were stolen in Durban in May. Both cars have not been recovered. MABUSI: I just want to know how come it takes them three hours to get to the car INT3 M9 KESHIA: We only actually got an alert an hour after the vehicle was physical taken away from our yard. INT1 M6 END VO: Keshia Chetty’s family Hilux was fitted with a Netstar Early Warning system and an additional back up unit. On the neighbour’s CCTV footage you can see the bakkie being moved down the road by the thieves – take note of the time – 22.56 . KESHIA: After that we got a phone call around 23.40 to say, to ask whether my brother who is the primary driver of the vehicle was ok? And whether the vehicle was ok // for us that was a bit of a shock – because an early warning system means… DEVI: it means early warning… KESHIA: early warning, //INT1 M6 VO: The two tracking devices were recovered about 40 km away in Kwamakhutha, south of Durban, almost two hours after the vehicle was stolen. Mabusi Khuzwayo’s Etios was stolen in the early hours of the morning. Although she didn’t have an early warning system, a battery tamper notification was picked up by Netstar at 02.15 am – the message went unnoticed, no teams were dispatched at the time. Mabusi only realised the car was missing just over an hour later. MABUSI: I phoned Netstar to say the car is missing //it was half past 3 am INT1 M4 VO: Mabusi was told a team was dispatched. She picked up her car’s location on the Netstar app, about an hour away from Durban in iFafa. But the response team only located the unit over three hours later. MABUSI: // the time they got to the car at 7, something to 7 the car was not there – //It took you this long to get to the car – what do you expect? INT1 M12 VO: What Netstar clients expect, is simply what they are promised. // UPSOUND NETSTAR CALL CENTRE: +/- 01.29: “We still have the largest private dedicated air and ground service in Southern Africa.” VO: According to their website their recovery teams are exclusive to Netstar, and their highly trained recovery personnel respond to incidents at immediate notice. But things have changed in recent months – Netstar have a new national recovery contractor, Rentrak. While Gauteng seems to be running more smoothly, there appears to be hiccups in some of the other provinces . INSIDER: we do recoveries for several different tracking companies – not just Nestar. INT1 M11 VO: We spoke to an insider who does vehicle recoveries for Rentrak in KwaZulu Natal – for fear of retribution we have hidden his identity. DEVI: Which one do you do first? INSIDER: You do the one that comes first. // if you are doing a track for another company and a Netstar comes // Netstar will have to wait. INT1 M12 VO: Rentrak took over Netstar’s national recovery operations during March and April. The company provides recovery services to a number of tracking companies across South Africa. Up until then, Dale Milcher exclusively did Netstar’s recoveries in Gauteng, Bloemfontein and Kimberly – he lost the contract after 22 years and had to close his doors at a cost of R2.5 million. DEVI: do you feel that the best bidder won? DALE: honestly? No. DEVI: Isn’t this just a case of sourgrapes – you didn’t get the contract DALE: // Sure I am upset, but it doesn’t change a thing // INT 1 M19 // the facts are the facts. INT 2 M33 // Their agents in the areas are doing work for everybody – some of them have got private jobs. // INT 1 M18// LINK: Not everyone can do armed vehicle recoveries - there are rules and regulations guiding the industry – not only to safeguard the people doing the work, but to ensure that consumers get the best service . VO: While PSIRA is the Private Security Industry Regulatory body - Netstar set their own ground rules in the Technical Mandatory Requirements section of their tender document: “The bidder’s armed response officers must at least have a grade C security grading in line with PSIRA requirements as well as an armed response certification.” This would apply to the contractor and its subcontractors. Our investigation revealed that Rentrak uses some recovery agents that don’t meet those requirements - some of these agents work on Netstar Recoveries. Rentrak supplied us with the PSIRA certificates for its subcontracted agents outside of Gauteng acknowledging that their “agents are not full time agents” and that they conduct other businesses such as farming. Of the 75 agents, only 22 complied 100% with the requirements . VO: One of the people that appeared on the Rentrak Recovery Agents Whatsapp Group is Gordon van Tonder – an electrician and police reservist in East London – he has not been PSIRA registered or graded. He has yet to do a call out, but is on currently standby. UPSOUND GORDON VAN TONDER – DEVI (CALLS TO AGENTS – CLIP….26) TIME CODE 14.40.58 DEVI: // if you are involved in any vehicle recovery, you would have to be registered with PSIRA before you do that. GORDON: I didn’t realise that // The chap you must be speak to is Darron Saayman – he’s got the contract 14.39.27 DEVI: Helping out? GORDON: I’m help him out yah. VO: Rentrak says that Gordon will not be dispatched until he’s done his registration and training. Darron Saayman is sub-contracted by another Rentrak sub-contractor. He has a PSIRA E grade – while he is a police reservist with 15 years experience…. His E grade qualifies him just to do basic patrolling – not even access control guarding. UPSOUND DARRON SAAYMAN - (CALLS TO AGENTS – CLIP….27) 14.44.55 DEVI: you are listed as an E grade at PSIRA, I’ve seen it – you need to have C grade – E is the bottom DARRON: No, no I know that, just please listen to my side – we’ve done our C grade, //, the course reports would have submitted I don’t know how long that process takes… DEVI: The point still remains you are doing recoveries for Rentrak and until PSIRA recognises what you have submitted to them – you are still on E grade DARRON: Correct VO: PSIRA is currently also investigating these apparent irregularities. Advocate Linda Mbana heads up law enforcement at the regulator. She says the rules are clear when it comes vehicle recovery. ADV MBANA: You must have Grade C – if you have Grade C that means you can do armed response – but you must also do armed response courses as well as firearm courses – so it is a package. INT1 M46 DEVI: Why so tough? ADV MBANA: risky VO: We also discovered that 37 of Rentrak’s subcontracted agents currently have no armed response training listed on the PSIRA database. Rentrack declined an on-camera interview but in correspondence said that an unarmed agent does not need an armed response grading. That would mean that of Rentrak’s 75 subcontracted agents, more than half are possibly doing recoveries unarmed. But even then PSIRA requires all security personal doing response work, armed or not, to have response training. Of the 75 subcontracted agents, at least 19 of them were listed as unemployed in the security industry. LINK: Being listed on PSIRA as unemployed doesn’t sound like a big deal - but it means you shouldn’t be working in the security industry you certainly wont have access to a company issued fire arm, so you would either be carrying your own or go in unarmed. VO: Even though our insider has had the appropriate training, he carries his own private firearm. DEVI: Can you use your own private firearm? ADV MBANA: // the employer, which is the business, the security service provider is supposed to furnish the employee // with firearms – the employee is not supposed to be utilising his or her private firearm. INT1 M36 VO: While Rentrak say that they have “no control over how PSIRA lists agents” - Adv Mbana says it’s the responsibility of employers to update employment status on the database ADV MBANA: // in terms of our regulation 8 – it is a misconduct for a particular service provider not to indicate to us how many intakes that particular company has taken. INT1 M16 VO: Rentrack say that subcontracted agents must at all times comply with all laws and regulations. They further stated that the bid process was lawful and has never been challenged. They deny any irregularities relating to their agents, stating that they have co-operated fully with the ongoing PSIRA investigation. They added that they are contractually prohibited from commenting on Netstar cases. According to Rentrak, besides E grade Darron Saayman, all of their agents are PSIRA registered as grade C and above. But that’s not the case. Their own list revealed another four D grade agents. Rentrak claimed these people were in the process of upgrading to C level. We checked the list of non-compliant agents with PSIRA, who confirmed that until applications are validated, the current gradings have been captured accurately. Netstar’s Managing Director Pierre Bruwer agreed to an interview. DEVI: Are you happy that your contractor has complied? PIERRE: in terms of submissions – and the high level requirements of netstar perspective we were comfortable that Rentrak is the most suitable supplier of our recovery service – // 15.59.17 DEVI: Does netstar have a dedicated ground and air teams? PIERRE: In certain areas we do, in other areas we share. // 14.58.50 VO: While Netstar’s recovery services through Rentrak are not 100% exclusive, the insider says it seems the size of the ground teams have also changed. INSIDER: sometimes in the vehicle there is only one person – like the driver he will handle all the equipment and do the recovery on his own // INT1 M42 // there is no day shift or night shift – you work 24 hours a day INT1 M14 VO: In Netstar’s tender document the minimum services required were quite clear - at least two trained and armed security officers would be needed per ground team. PIERRE: From a tender perspective we put out a guideline to say at least two people per team – in certain areas we require one, so it was merely a guideline. 15.03.06 VO: However, Netstar insists there are now more teams on the ground and that the recovery stats have improved with Rentrak. Looking at KZN, there were 11 teams of two people, with day and night shifts in Durban, Pietermaritzburg and Richardsbay previously. PIERRE: today we have 18 supporting us from a recovery vehicles 15.52 DEVI: two people? PIERRE: not all of the them are two people, some of them one people – // 15.52.50 //the teams today could be a person supported by SAPS we refer to it as 18 teams on the ground 15.54.00 VO: We wanted to verify the information and requested detailed statistics along with the details of the new agents - during the interview Bruwer was more than willing to share this with us, but afterwards said that the specific information was confidential. Netstar is adamant that their footprint has increased nationally. DEVI: increased numbers – don’t comply PIERRE: that’s the response that we are awaiting from PSIRA and Rentrak//16.31.46 VO: But clients like Keshia and Mabusi are still waiting for answers. Bruwer is believes that Netstar complied in both incidents - he confirmed Mabusi’s case was being investigated as it appears the agent didn’t respond in time. KESHIA: // I think it was a sense of being // taken for a ride – because you are lead to believe you are taking a contract for X but you’re actually getting Y // INT1 M7 VO: PSIRA says it’s committed to getting to the bottom of the allegations against Rentrak and its subcontractors and hope to wrap up their investigations soon. ADV MBANA: // We don’t tolerate non-compliance// there is going to be fireworks. INT1 M57 END PROMOS PROMO 1 VO: Vehicle tracking device are a necessity in South Africa’s crime climate. But will your car be recovered? We investigate irregularities behind one big tracking company’s apparent false promises. PROMO 2 VO: Clients are promised exclusive ground and air recovery teams for stolen vehicles, but a special investigation reveals irregularities behind one major tracking company’s recovery operations. PROMO 3 VO: Exclusive ground and air recovery teams to recover your vehicle when it’s stolen - that’s the promise one tracking company makes to its clients, but is it what customers are getting? metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Netstar dupes clients into thinking they have exclusive and private ground and air recovery teams – we investigate a string of irregularities behind a big corporate’s false promises.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: - Consumers being screwed - Corporates being called out on their lies - Action packed footage
metadata.Summary: Netstar restructured its recovery team business model – they gave contractors of 23 years the boot and opened the door to new blood – cutting costs and apparently improving their business model – but is that what’s really happening? They’ve cut down recovery teams, appointed a contractor that employs plumbers, mechanics, active duty cops, unregistered and suspended PSIRA companies. And consumers are none the wiser – they’re still paying the same fees, but not getting the same service. We lift the lid on apparent sub-standard service that leaving consumers bearing the brunt of it.
metadata.Further information: Up until February 2019 Netstar used to have sub-contractors in each province with dedicated teams. They used to get a sizable retainer and be paid a minimal fee per call out. The number of teams were determined by Netstar. Some companies had worked for Netstar for 23 and 10 years respectively. Last year, Netstar decided that they wanted recoveries teams to fall under one entity nationally and put out a tender. The contract was awarded to a company called Rentrack – they have a national footprint – but it’s not exclusive to Netstar - they do recoveries for Matrix, C-Track and Tracker. IRREGULARITIES 1. NOT EXCLUVIE RECOVERY TEAMS – NETSTAR PROMISE TO CLIENTS - We have cases where multiple cars from different tracking companies were taken on the same day in May – four Netstar cars were lost. The other companies cars were recovered – same team – too many recoveries. 2. EMPLOYS COPS TO DO RECOVERIES – ILLEGAL FOR COPS TO DO OTHER WORK 3. EMPLOYEES NOT ALL PSIRA REGISTERED – REQUIREMENT OF NETSTAR 4. EMPLOYS PEOPLE WITH NO SECURITY HISTORY – A PLUMBER / A MECHANIC 5. SUB-CONTRACTS COMPANIES THAT HAVE BEEN SUSPENDED FROM PSIRA – RED FLAG!!! 6. DOES NOT HAVE ENOUGH FIREARMS REGISTERED WITH SAPS – SO THESE COMPANIES ARE USING PRIVATE FIREARMS 7. POLICE CLEARANCE FOR EVERYONE COULD NOT HAVE BEEN DONE – NETSTAR REQUIREMENT * HOW DO WE KNOW THESE THINGS? - We have an insider that works for the new company feeding us information of the recovery team whatsapp group and has first hand experience with these recoveries gone wrong. - We have insiders in Netstar that have given us the recovery stats - We have pulled the data of PSIRA’s online platform – it’s not a case of outdated information – these details are updated real time by companies themselves - We have checked the firearm registration this week. - We have audio recordings confirming employment CASE STUDY 1 Balan Chetty’s Hilux was stolen in Durban in April – he had two tracking devices installed because he new the Hilux was a high risk vehicle. He has CCTV footage of this car being stolen. Netstar only picked up the car had been stolen an hour later despite having an Early Warning System installed – the car was not recovered – they are furious and outraged having learnt that they’ve been paying service that NEtstar no longer provides. CASE STUDY 2 4 MAY – 4 Netstar cars were stolen in KZN – not one recovered – on the same day – the same recovery team recovered a car for C-Track. The customers are furious! Two of the cars belonged to Crawford College – Rentrack didn’t send a recovery team – firstly because they didn’t have a team available, secondly they said they will only go when a signal is received from the unit – despite it being reported by the clients – this would not have happened under the old system. INSIDER We have someone who works for the new company – he’s seen first hand how backwards everything has gone – how the one and only team they have in Durban purposely delays reporting recoveries to push up the hours they can charge for. He’s seen how many cars they are losing because they are servicing different companies and has personally spoken to the Netstar control centre who have complained about losses. EX-EMPLOYEE Will explain the danger and importance of properly trained recovery teams. FORMER SUB-CONTRACTOR Will explain the break down of how it used to work and what’s happening now as well as point out irregularities in the tender process. CONFRONTS The main confronts are NOT with the employees – but with the company that is subcontracting them – so we are putting the allegations to Rentrack. In terms of the employees, we are merely confirming that the teams are not qualified and using private fire arms. Rentrack has to answer for employing them and seemingly misleading Netstar. Essentially the unqualified people aren’t lying about their qualifications, it’s there for the world to see on the PSIRA public online platform – it’s Rentrack and essentially Netstar that didn’t do due diligence. This is how I think it could work best in terms of storytelling and trying to keep costs down as I also understand that travel budgets are limited and it won’t be possible to go to all these places (Uitenhage, Plett, Bloem & Durbs) to have a 10 min chat to these teams. Netstar’s interview will focus on whether they aware of what is going is on with their new contractor – were they hoodwinked and what will they do to rectify the illegality and substandard service? VISUALS I have a lot of recent footage of action packed vehicle recoveries, re-enactments of hijackings and vehicle thefts – there is also a lot of CCTV footage of cars being stolen and hijacked – so visually it would be action packed and fast paced with new footage. IRREGULARITIES – VISUAL DEVICE Then to introduce the problem areas and unqualified teams I’d work with an editor to use a clever device using maps and their photos, bringing up qualifications and short comings in a slick graphic representation. We’d then have audio recordings that we use along with the graphic and audio wave to make it visually interesting.
